cards.title: Iran says the Hormuz draft is in its final stage, but reopening is unconfirmed
cards.summary: AP reported that Iran described the Oman talks as being in the final drafting stage; the operating terms and timing of any reopening remain unsettled.
detail: AP reported on Wednesday that Iran said it was in the final stage of drafting an agreement with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz. The report also said talks between Lebanese and Israeli negotiators continued in Rome as violence tested a shaky ceasefire in southern Lebanon.

The Hormuz track matters because the waterway is a major energy and cargo route whose disruption has raised fuel, shipping, and inflation pressure well beyond the region. A draft is not the same as a signed, operational arrangement.

The next evidence is an official text, actual vessel movement, and whether the U.S., Iranian, Omani, and Gulf accounts converge on the terms. The separate Lebanon escalation is a reminder that regional de-escalation remains uneven.

cards.title: ECB policy remains the euro-area driver behind the market snapshot
cards.summary: The ECB’s latest policy setting remains the key euro-area reference while markets absorb lower oil and improved global risk appetite.
detail: The euro-area driver card remains anchored to the ECB’s latest policy communication and the euro-area data calendar. Wednesday’s global move does not by itself establish a new ECB decision.
The connection to markets is through inflation, growth, and the cost of credit. Lower oil can ease one pressure, while geopolitical and trade uncertainty can still affect the outlook.
The next evidence is the next ECB communication and Eurostat release, alongside the European market close. No rate path or investment view is inferred here.
cards.why: Provides a source-backed market snapshot without investment advice.

cards.title: Asian shares reverse lower as the Kospi drops 4.5% before payrolls
cards.summary: AP reported a mostly lower Asian session on Thursday, led by a 4.5% Kospi fall as chip stocks declined and investors reduced risk ahead of Friday’s U.S. jobs report.
detail: AP reported that Asian shares were mostly lower on Thursday, with South Korea’s Kospi falling 4.5% to 6,306.40. The report said oil was near $79 a barrel and that uncertainty around the Iran war and Hormuz reopening remained over markets.

The regional move contrasts with the prior U.S. record-area close: chip and other technology names were under pressure as investors took profits and reduced risk before the U.S. employment report. That is a description of the session, not a forecast for the region.
The next evidence is the regional close, Friday’s payrolls report, and any official update on Hormuz shipping. Currency and policy signals remain relevant for Japan and other Asian markets.
cards.why: Replaces the prior Asian-gains snapshot with the current session’s verified reversal and a named reason for the move.
